name: Flutter
summary: A cross-platform reactive UI toolkit in which immutable Dart widgets configure element and render-object trees, the framework performs layout and composition, and an engine/embedder boundary turns frames and platform input into native application output.

features.name: Immutable widget declarations
features.description: Flutter widgets are immutable descriptions of UI composition. The framework compares widget configurations and maintains separate element and render-object structures for lifecycle, layout, painting, and interaction.
benefits: Uses one declarative description for creation and update
costs: Rebuild frequency and identity affect update work
Application state must be represented outside immutable widget configuration

features.name: Render-object layout and painting pipeline
features.description: Flutter's rendering layer builds a tree of RenderObjects responsible for layout, painting, hit testing, and accessibility; the framework updates this tree as widget configuration changes.
benefits: Separates declarative composition from concrete layout and painting
Supports custom render objects and platform-independent controls
costs: Multiple trees create synchronization and lifecycle work
Layout constraints and paint invalidation must be honored

features.name: Engine and embedder platform boundary
features.description: The Flutter engine rasterizes composited scenes and exposes low-level primitives through dart:ui, while a platform-specific embedder coordinates rendering surfaces, accessibility, input, and the native event loop.
benefits: Shares framework semantics across supported platforms
Keeps operating-system integration behind an explicit boundary
costs: Platform capabilities and embedder behavior remain target-specific
Cross-boundary integration adds packaging and scheduling constraints

mathematical_views.question: How does a new immutable widget tree induce updates to the existing element and render-object trees?
assumptions: Widget identity and type guide correspondence
The framework reconciles only affected subtrees
The view abstracts Dart object allocation and garbage collection

mathematical_views.question: How do widget state, layout invalidation, compositing, engine rasterization, and embedder presentation relate during a frame?
assumptions: Each layer exposes a boundary to the next
A frame may omit unchanged work
The view models architecture rather than proving timing guarantees

costs: Rebuild and identity behavior must be understood
Tree lifecycle and invalidation are complex
